L3Harris statement (Nov. 14): supporting the FAA investigation; more than 70% of copper-to-fiber conversion complete,"In a written statement on its newsroom, L3Harris said it has been modernizing the communications infrastructure supporting the National Airspace System with the FAA and its telco partners, has completed ""more than 70%"" of the planned conversion from legacy copper wires to fiber, is ""supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop,"" and ""takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously."" It does not address the remote-site router, contractor error, or a faulty device. NPR and Reuters (via CNA) report the same statement. [L3Harris statement](https://www.l3harris.com/newsroom/press-release/2026/11/l3harris-statement-nov-13-ground-stop) · [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/14/nx-s1-6040952/faa-ground-stop-airplane-travel) · [CNA (Reuters)](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/us-aviation-shutdown-blamed-l3-harris-installed-router-6552171)"
"DOT written release of the Saturday briefing remarks (Duffy): router flooded the network with over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds","DOT posted Duffy's Saturday remarks in writing. He said that in ""at least one"" remote FAA location, L3Harris (which he said owns the FAA's ATC network) was doing routine maintenance to move lines from copper to fiber (TDM to IP); ""either through contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment,"" the router ""started flooding other routers in our air traffic control system"" with ""over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds,"" disrupting communications with aircraft and some radar feeds. ""We haven't determined what the fault was."" On cyber: ""we don't believe this was cyber at all."" This is the officials' account in writing, not an FAA root-cause report; the FAA newsroom statement is still the preliminary Friday one. [DOT release](https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/icymi-us-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-provides-update-restoration-airspace) · [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/air-transport/safety-ops-regulation/faa-says-router-malfunction-led-ground-stop)"`,

old_string: headline,"The nationwide ground stop was cancelled at 8:16 PM ET Friday (FAA Advisory 005). At a Saturday 10:30 AM ET DOT briefing with FAA Administrator Bedford, Duffy said the outage began while contractor L3Harris was switching lines from copper to fiber at a remote FAA site, and a router involved in the work flooded the network; officials have not determined whether the router was faulty or the contractor erred. Officials say there is no sign of a cyberattack. More than 4,000 US flights were cancelled Saturday as of 10:50 AM ET."
